extracted.intended_audience: students of Math 216 / graduate or advanced undergraduate students of algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the textbook definitions, equivalent criteria, and structural properties for ampleness/very-ampleness/semiample line bundles, the Curve-to-Projective Extension Theorem, gluing of schemes, the Grassmannian (functor, representability, Plücker embedding), and the relative Spec/Proj constructions. Intended for learning and applying these concepts in scheme-theoretic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing of schemes (fibered coproduct / glued scheme)
rubrics_metrics.description: This construction is a fibered coproduct in the category of schemes (and locally ringed spaces); the resulting cofibered diagram is also a fibered diagram. Unlike products, fibered coproducts don't exist in general in the category of schemes, but for the scheme-theoretic gluing described here the construction behaves well with respect to base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: (a) One can prove the fibered coproduct property if desired. (b) Interesting questions: can we recover the gluing locus from the glued scheme and the two closed subschemes? (Yes.) When is a scheme the gluing of two closed subschemes along their scheme-theoretic intersection? (When their scheme-theoretic union is the entire scheme.) (c) Gluing a scheme to itself along isomorphic disjoint closed subschemes may not be possible as a scheme; one may get an algebraic space instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties preserved under gluing (Exercise 16.4.O)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X1 and X2 are glued along closed subschemes via φ to form X1 ⊔_φ X2, then several properties of the Xi are inherited by the glued scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements to prove: (a) If X1 and X2 are universally closed then the glued scheme is universally closed. (b) If X1 and X2 are separated then the glued scheme is separated. (c) If X1 and X2 are finite type over a Noetherian ring A then the glued scheme is of finite type (hint: reduce to affine case, choose generators of the algebras and ideals and show certain generators generate the relation ring). Conclude that if X1 and X2 are proper then their gluing is proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curve-to-Projective Extension Theorem (16.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose C is a pure dimension 1 Noetherian scheme over an affine base S, and p is a regular closed point of C. If Y is a projective S-scheme, then any morphism C \ {p} → Y (of S-schemes) extends to all of C. Extension, if it exists, is unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical use: typically with S = Spec k and C a k-variety. Notes on uniqueness: reduce to reduced neighborhood of p and use that maps from reduced schemes to separated schemes are determined by their behavior on a dense open. Central idea of proof: 'clear denominators' — reduce to Y = P^n, pick a uniformizer t at p, interpret map as n+1 rational functions with no common zeros on C \ {p}, choose N = min(val_p(fi)) and form t^{-N} fi to obtain global sections giving the extended map. Exercises show necessity of hypotheses: projectivity of Y, one-dimensionality and non-singularity of C are necessary (counterexamples provided). A valuative criterion of properness can weaken projectivity to properness with more work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'very ample' (relative / π-very ample)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given π: X → Spec A proper and L an invertible sheaf on X, L is very ample over A (π-very ample, relatively very ample) if X ≅ Proj S• for some finitely generated graded ring S• over A generated in degree 1 and L ≅ O_Proj S•(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common shorthand: say 'very ample' when the structure morphism is clear. Existence of a very ample line bundle implies X is projective. Equivalent formulation (Exercise 16.6.A): L is very ample iff the complete linear series |L| gives a closed embedding X → P^n_A for some n. Also: very ample implies base-point-free (Exercise 16.6.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactions of very ample and base-point-free (Exercises 16.6.B and 16.6.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Very ample implies base-point-free; conversely, tensoring a base-point-free line bundle with a very ample one gives a very ample bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.6.C: If L is very ample and M is base-point-free on a proper A-scheme X, then L ⊗ M is very ample. Hint: use embeddings given by L and M, form product map and use Segre/Cancellation Theorem to obtain an embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and equivalent conditions for 'ample' (Theorem 16.6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let π: X → Spec A be proper and L an invertible sheaf on X. The following are equivalent characterizations of L being ample over A: (a) For some N>0, L^⊗N is very ample over A (and a' states: for all n≫0, L^⊗n is very ample). (b) For all finite type quasicoherent sheaves F, there exists n0 such that for n≥n0, F ⊗ L^⊗n is globally generated. (c) As f runs over all global sections of L^⊗n (n>0), the open subsets X_f = {p | f(p) ≠ 0} form a base for the topology of X. (c') The affines among the X_f form a base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These different flavors connect projective geometry ((a),(a')), global generation/stalkwise condition (b), and topological conditions (c),(c'). Remarks: (a)/(a') relate to projective geometry; (b) to global generation; (c)/(c') are topological and make no reference to π. Consequences: (a) implies (b) (Serre's Theorem A), Kodaira-type analytic criteria exist in the complex category. The proof sketch in the Noetherian case is given, with notes where Noetherian hypotheses are used and how to remove them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic consequences and permanence properties of ampleness (Exercises 16.6.E–16.6.I,16.6.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various useful facts about ample/very ample line bundles used repeatedly throughout algebraic geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (16.6.E) If L is ample on proper A-scheme X, then for n≫0, L^⊗n ⊗ M is very ample for any invertible M. (16.6.F) Every line bundle on a projective A-scheme is the difference of two very ample line bundles (L ≅ M ⊗ N^∨). (16.6.G) If π: X' → Y is finite morphism of proper A-schemes and L is ample on Y, then π^*L is ample on X'; proof uses Theorem 16.6.2(b) and behavior of pushforward/pullback. (16.6.H/16.6.I) Tensor sums and fiber products: ampleness is preserved under tensoring with ample or base-point-free sheaves, and under certain product constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiample line bundles (16.6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L is semiample if some tensor power L^⊗N is base-point-free (i.e., some power gives a morphism to projective space, not necessarily an embedding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation: very ample ⇔ some power gives closed embedding; semiample ⇔ some power gives morphism to projective space. The text notes the notion but says it will not be used here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampleness in the absolute (quasicompact) setting (16.6.5,16.6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ampleness can be defined without reference to a structure morphism: for L invertible on a quasicompact scheme X, L is ample iff the sets X_f (f ranging over sections of L^⊗n for n>0) form a base for the topology of X. Theorem 16.6.6 gives equivalent statements in the quasicompact/quasiseparated setting analogous to Theorem 16.6.2, including a graded ring criterion (d): letting S• = ⊕_{n≥0} Γ(X,L^⊗n), the Proj construction yields an open embedding X → Proj S• (warning: S• need not be finitely generated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: on an affine scheme every invertible sheaf is ample; on a projective A-scheme O(1) is ample. Part (d) implies separatedness of X. The equivalences mirror the relative case but are phrased absolutely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grassmannian functor definition (16.7.0.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed n and k, the Grassmannian functor G(k,n) sends a scheme B to the set of locally free rank-k quotients Q of O_B^⊕n (up to isomorphism). Equivalently one can parameterize short exact sequences 0 → S → O_B^⊕n → Q → 0 with S locally free of rank n−k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: prefer quotients rather than subobjects because kernels of surjections of locally free sheaves are locally free, whereas cokernels of injections need not be. The k=1 case recovers maps to P^{n-1} via Theorem 16.4.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of the Grassmannian (cover by standard open subfunctors)
rubrics_metrics.description: G(k,n) is a Zariski sheaf and is covered by open subfunctors G(k,n)_I, where I ranges over k-subsets of {1,...,n}; on G(k,n)_I the chosen k sections are linearly independent. After renaming summands one may assume I = {1,...,k} and show G(k,n)_I ≅ A^{k(n−k)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: in the trivializing neighborhood the surjection is represented by an n×k matrix; the locus where the k×k minor for columns I is invertible defines G(k,n)_I. On that patch, the remaining columns give k(n−k) functions providing a map to A^{k(n−k)}, and conversely these functions reconstruct the surjection. Gluing these affines yields G(k,n), showing it is representable, smooth and irreducible of dimension k(n−k) over a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal exact sequence over the Grassmannian (16.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a tautological exact sequence on G(k,n): 0 → S → O_{G(k,n)}^⊕n → Q → 0, where Q is the universal rank-k quotient and S the universal rank-(n−k) subbundle (kernel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This universal sequence encodes the moduli interpretation and is used to construct the Plücker embedding and other universal constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plücker embedding and Plücker equations (16.7.2–16.7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying ∧^k to the universal surjection O^⊕n → Q gives a surjection O^⊕(n choose k) → det Q, hence a map G(k,n) → P^{N−1} (N = n choose k), called the Plücker embedding. The homogeneous quadratic relations among the Plücker coordinates are the Plücker relations; these cut out G(k,n) inside projective space (though proving generating property of the ideal requires further work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises: show explicit relations (e.g., for G(2,4) the single quadratic x12x34 − x13x24 + x14x23 = 0 cuts out the image); analyze consequences such as rulings on quadrics and identify G(2,4) with a smooth quadric in P^5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further Grassmannian properties and generalizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Group action, bundles, and partial flag varieties: GL_n acts on G(k,n); one can define Grassmannian bundles G(k,F) for a rank-n locally free sheaf F over a base X; the construction behaves well under base change and generalizes to partial flag varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises indicate to check GL_n-action via functor language; define G(k,F) as a representable functor gluing relative copies of the standard affine patches; partial flag varieties follow similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Spec of a quasicoherent sheaf of algebras (17.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a scheme X and a quasicoherent O_X-algebra B, one can form β: Spec B → X which is affine over X and satisfies the universal property that for any µ: W → X, X-morphisms W → Spec B correspond to O_X-algebra maps B → µ_* O_W (equivalently maps µ^* B → O_W).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete description: on any affine open Spec A ⊂ X, Γ(Spec A,B) is an A-algebra, and above that open the construction coincides with Spec of that algebra. Existence is shown by gluing local affine Specs using the universal property. Proposition 17.1.3: restriction to an open U ⊂ X gives Spec(B|_U) which satisfies the universal property over U.
